original_value: AbstractData science skills are rapidly becoming a necessity in modern science. In response to this need, institutions and organizations around the world are developing research data science curricula to teach the programming and computational skills that are needed to build and maintain data infrastructures and maximize the use of available data. To date, however, few of these courses have included an explicit ethics component, and developing such components can be challenging. This paper describes a novel approach to teaching data ethics on short courses developed for the CODATA-RDA Schools for Research Data Science. The ethics content of these schools is centred on the concept of open and responsible (data) science citizenship that draws on virtue ethics to promote ethics of practice. Despite having little formal teaching time, this concept of citizenship is made central to the course by distributing ethics content across technical modules. Ethics instruction consists of a wide range of techniques, including stand-alone lectures, group discussions and mini-exercises linked to technical modules. This multi-level approach enables students to develop an understanding both of “responsible and open (data) science citizenship”, and of how such responsibilities are implemented in daily research practices within their home environment. This approach successfully locates ethics within daily data science practice, and allows students to see how small actions build into larger ethical concerns. This emphasises that ethics are not something “removed from daily research” or the remit of data generators/end users, but rather are a vital concern for all data scientists.

result.paraphrase: Abstract data science skills are quickly becoming essential in modern science. In response, institutions and organizations worldwide are designing research data science curricula to teach the programming and computational skills needed to build and maintain data infrastructures and make the most of available data. So far, however, few of these courses have included an explicit ethics component, and creating such components can be difficult. This paper presents a novel method for teaching data ethics in short courses developed for the CODATA-RDA Schools for Research Data Science. The schools’ ethics content centers on the idea of open and responsible (data) science citizenship, drawing on virtue ethics to encourage ethics of practice. Although formal teaching time is limited, this citizenship concept is integrated into the course by spreading ethics content across technical modules. Ethics teaching uses a range of methods, including standalone lectures, group discussions, and mini-exercises tied to technical modules. This multi-level approach helps students understand both “responsible and open (data) science citizenship” and how such responsibilities are carried out in everyday research practice in their home setting. In doing so, it successfully embeds ethics in everyday data science work and helps students see how small actions accumulate into larger ethical issues. This underscores that ethics are not something “removed from daily research” or the sole responsibility of data generators/end users, but instead a vital concern for all data scientists.
